published_text: A cell at a ceiling records only that the limit was reached. Count cells at the extreme before any aggregation and analyse only the ones that moved.

faults.definition: Writing a failure mode down did not stop it
published_text: And the strongest evidence for this entry is this document. Mode 21 above — four outcomes collapsed into two — was written here and published, and committed again two hours later in the next experiment, with five outcomes in one bin: a wrong category, a legitimate absence, a task never attempted, an empty reply, and the reader being blind to the construction. Four facts about the subject and one about the instrument, in one column. The document was accurate, published, and had no effect, because a catalogue occupies no position in the pipeline. It is reference material, and reference material depends on recall at the moment of writing, which is exactly when context is thinnest. Knowing this failure mode did not prevent it here. What prevented it afterwards was a module that refuses to accept a bin named none, other or silent at all, and asserts that the declared outcomes are exhaustive and disjoint before it will return a table — described in the companion document. The lesson is not to read harder.

And it is not only documents. The same thing happens to a named instrument. Our tooling prints a roster of available instruments at the top of every single exchange, read live from the source so it cannot drift. On the day described above, the instrument built for exactly the reading in hand was in that roster dozens of times and its implementation was a day old. We built a new one instead — and the one we built was a verdict machine, entry 44. A roster entry is not an instrument: a one-line label reads as a name, and a name is something you recognise rather than something you reach for. Recognition is not retrieval, and the moment of needing a different ruler is the moment of lowest attention. The cause was structural and cheap to fix, which is the companion document's business rather than this one's: the corrective procedure loaded the papers saying which error this is and not the sheet saying which instrument to use instead, so it diagnosed and never re-armed.

The uncomfortable one. Over three days, 96 pushbacks. The density of replies flagged for a two-option frame across those three days: 0.79, 0.69, 0.88 per thousand words, each day within one width of the day before (widths as in entry 24). Against the first two days pooled, a comparison chosen after the data, the third day ran at 1.24 times the rate, exact 95 per cent interval 0.76 to 1.99, so a fall of more than 24 per cent by the third day is outside what was measured. (The scanner's precision on this author is 20 to 35 per cent: 4 or 7 of 20 flagged frames were real two-option reductions, on two separate readings. Its rate on human-written prompts is 0.28 to 0.58 per thousand words. The level is not a count of real frames, and the comparison across days assumes the precision held steady across them.) The corrections landed one at a time, and the rate shows no change that clears its own width. A guard is a filter, not a teacher, and expecting it to teach is how it gets removed for underperforming at a job it never had.

faults.name: A result that does not resolve, filed as a null
faults.definition: A result that does not resolve, filed as a null
published_text: A test returns a p-value above the threshold and the finding is recorded as no effect. It is not a statement about the world. It is a statement about the ruler's reach. A quantity that cannot be resolved at the sample size available has not been shown to be absent. Nothing has been shown at all, and the honest report is a position rather than a verdict.

Ours: a rate measured either side of a hardware failure came back at p = 0.178 on 25 observations a side and went into the record as a null. The reading it actually had was a direction — the rate had moved the opposite way from what we expected — and a position on an axis. Both were discarded to produce one bit.

And the obvious fix is the same failure wearing a lab coat. Asked to do better, we built a power calculator: given this distribution, how many samples before a move of size X clears the threshold. That is the verdict machine with extra steps. It still terminates in a two-outcome test, it hardcodes a significance level and a power target — two more constants chosen by the observer — and it wraps the verdict in several hundred repetitions of itself. It was deleted rather than kept, because the artifact to be refused was the verdict, not the sample size. The replacement for a verdict is a position, not a better verdict.

guards.name: The ruler is chosen before the quantity is computed
published_text: The default move is a value with a standard error, which answers one kind of question and quietly refuses all the others. So a roster of available rulers is placed in front of the model at the start of every single exchange, automatically, read live from the source document rather than from a copy: the separation of setup from signal, the width needed to exclude a runner-up, the profile that places unlike records on one axis without assuming a shared mechanism, the three-seat reading of one event, the integration time beyond which phase becomes noise, the corner where neither a count nor a phase resolves, and the test of whether two effects add or multiply.

Why it is injected rather than remembered. A roster in a document is consulted when the model thinks to consult it, which is precisely never at the moment it is needed. Injected at the top of every exchange it costs nothing and arrives before the framing is fixed. The guard is the position, not the content.

guards.name: The instrument is tested as an object before it is pointed at anything
published_text: Every instrument is first run on a case it must pass and a case it must fail, and both results are recorded as numbers:

A ceiling — what the instrument reads on genuine, held-out examples of the thing it is meant to detect. Nothing can score better than that, and if the ceiling is low the instrument cannot be used at all, whatever it later reports. A floor, which is never assumed to be zero — what the instrument reads on material that by construction contains none of the target. It is always some small nonzero rate, and that rate is the bar everything else must clear. A known-good seat — a case so easy that failing it condemns the instrument. Four instruments in a row passed our own inspection and were later shown to be measuring proxies. Every one of them would have been caught in minutes by a known-good seat, and none of them had one.

Measured floors have twice told us the instrument itself was the result. In one case the detection rule matched ordinary material thousands of times per million words. The rule was rewritten and the rate fell by roughly three orders of magnitude. The floor measurement also reversed one of our own fixes — it showed that a refinement we had just made was cutting the most diagnostic cases while buying nothing at the scale we actually work at. A floor is not paperwork. It changes decisions.

published_text: The writer cannot hear its own register (Faults, entry 45), so the check is mechanical and runs in the site gate on every release of the business pages. Its record so far is in sample and says little. The phrase list was written from the copy it was then tested on: it passes the corrected site with no hits and catches that morning’s version 23 times, which any list fitted to its own examples would do. recount_requirements.name: Name the ruler before the number
recount_requirements.text: The instrument and the question it answers are named in the output, beside the figure, and were chosen before the quantity was computed.

recount_requirements.name: Write the baseline down first
recount_requirements.text: Sample counts, windows, averaging and the number of places examined are written down for every arm before the measurement arm is computed.

recount_requirements.name: State the data source
recount_requirements.text: Each input names where it came from. Raw copies of every source read are kept with their SHA-256 hashes.

recount_requirements.name: State the version read
recount_requirements.text: The version, edition or retrieval date of every source, and the version of this standard, are stated with the date and time of the read.

recount_requirements.name: Use reading outcomes
recount_requirements.text: Every reading is reported as ABOVE, BELOW, CONSISTENT or CANNOT_TELL against a figure, band or bound named in advance, with its edge convention, its tolerance for a point figure, and the size that matters where the reading is a departure from a null. Every CANNOT_TELL carries one reason from the closed list in section 6. A failed read of a source is reported as NOTHING_RETURNED.

recount_requirements.name: Give each reading its interval and level
recount_requirements.text: Every reading carries its interval, the method and the level of that interval, its n, and the n it was selected from where it is a selection. The method and level are named in the plan before the read. A changed level is a new reading and is reported beside the first. Every rate names its denominator.

recount_requirements.name: Test the instrument first
recount_requirements.text: The instrument is run on a case it must pass and a case it must fail before it is pointed at the claim. Both results are recorded.

recount_requirements.name: Publish receipts
recount_requirements.text: Every number in the recount links to the file, row or run it came from, so a reader can rerun it.

recount_requirements.name: Name dropped material
recount_requirements.text: Any run, row or arm that is discarded is named in the output with the reason and what replaced it.

recount_requirements.name: Publish corrections beside the first reading
recount_requirements.text: A reading that is later corrected stays in the record beside the correction and its reason.

recount_requirements.name: Keep CANNOT_TELL as its own result
recount_requirements.text: CANNOT_TELL is never folded into pass or fail, and never counted as agreement or as disagreement. The two guards cited here carry the principle of never folding and nothing else in this standard.

recount_requirements.name: State what was not tested
recount_requirements.text: The recount lists every code, fault and guard that was not tested and why. An entry marked NOT_APPLICABLE was tested for applicability and is listed with its reason.

recount_requirements.name: Print the counts beside every headline share
recount_requirements.text: Beside every headline share the recount prints the count of NOTHING_RETURNED and the share of CANNOT_TELL, split by reason. The reasons are the outcome reasons for readings and the status reasons for statuses.
